questions.q:
(a) Simplify (x² + 2x − 15)/(2x² − 7x + 3). [4]
(b) Show that (n + 3)² − (n − 3)² is a multiple of 12 for all integers n. [2]
ms: (a) M1: attempt to factorise 2x² − 7x + 3 into two brackets giving two of the three terms correctly
(b) M1: n² + 6n + 9 − (n² − 6n + 9), or uses difference of two squares (6)(2n)
(b) A1: = 12n, which is 12 × an integer, so a multiple of 12
questions.model:
(a) Numerator: x² + 2x − 15 = (x + 5)(x − 3).
Denominator: 2x² − 7x + 3 = (2x − 1)(x − 3).
Cancel (x − 3): the answer is (x + 5)/(2x − 1).
(b) (n + 3)² − (n − 3)² = n² + 6n + 9 − (n² − 6n + 9) = 12n.
n is an integer, so 12n is a multiple of 12.
questions.tip: Only cancel whole brackets that are factors of both the top and the bottom.

questions.q:
(a) Write 3/(x + 2) − (x − 4)/(x² − 4) as a single fraction in its simplest form. [4]
(b) Simplify (x² − 9)/(x + 1) ÷ (x − 3)/(x² + x). [3]
ms: (b) M1: inverts the second fraction and multiplies
(b) M1: factorises x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3) and x² + x = x(x + 1)
questions.model:
(a) x² − 4 = (x + 2)(x − 2), so the common denominator is (x + 2)(x − 2).
3/(x + 2) = 3(x − 2)/((x + 2)(x − 2))
Numerator: 3(x − 2) − (x − 4) = 3x − 6 − x + 4 = 2x − 2
Answer: (2x − 2)/((x + 2)(x − 2)) = 2(x − 1)/(x² − 4)
(b) (x − 3)(x + 3)/(x + 1) × x(x + 1)/(x − 3)
Cancel (x − 3) and (x + 1): the answer is x(x + 3).
questions.tip: When subtracting a fraction, put its numerator in a bracket: −(x − 4) = −x + 4.
